title: Identification and isolation of antibodies against pathogenic bacteria in healthy blood donors and infected patients
summary: Bacteria that are resistant to antibiotics are an increasing problem for health worldwide. Monoclonal antibodies may represent an alternative to antibiotics. As part of the project, human sera from healthy blood donors, infected patients and cystic fibrosis patients will be tested for antibacterial antibodies. If antibacterial antibodies are present, B cells will be isolated from the corresponding whole blood samples in order to clone and characterize these antibodies.

interventions.name: Identification of antibacterial antibodies in sera from cystic fibrosis patients. Isolation of such antibodies by single cell sorting of B cells after isolation of PBMC after blood collection.
Identification of antibacterial antibodies in sera from healthy blood donors. Isolation of such antibodies by single cell sorting of B cells after isolation of PBMC after blood collection.
Identification of antibacterial antibodies in sera from infected patients. Isolation of such antibodies by single cell sorting of B cells after isolation of PBMC after blood collection.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cystic fibrosis diagnosis OR infection with resistant bacteria OR healthy blood donor, clinically stable, able to give consent
Exclusion criteria:
incapable of giving consent, under 18 years old, clinically unstable
